We started seeing a significant increase in end-to-end latency and intermittent 5xx errors from the Redwood streaming endpoint used by our live ingestion pipeline (client SDK v1.4.2). - Client-side retries increase error rate and saturate our upstream queue

This is severe for us — periodic but recurring throughout the day. We need a priority investigation and any mitigation you can provide. Happy to jump on a call.

Team — forwarding MarketPlay's report. I reproduced a short run using their trace and the failure pattern looks like a header fragmentation / parser state issue in the client integration path. Notes from quick triage: 

- Repro: replaying their trace with small chunk sizes causes our streaming parser to emit a "parse: incomplete headers" error; downstream code falls back, triggers a 502-like response to the client and causes a retry storm.
- Observed on both proxy and direct route (so not exclusively a proxy bug).
- Affected SDK: client-sdk-js v1.4.2 (they say release).

Immediate asks:
1) Karthik — can you look at the dechunker / header reassembly state machine? My hunch is a race where header termination across chunk boundaries isn't treated atomically and the parser falls back to error mode.
2) Rishi — please coordinate with Ops to enable an edge reassembly rule and a temporary route to a more permissive model pool (lower QPS) to reduce retries.
3) Marissa — keep MarketPlay updated; they are sensitive to SLA impact.

Attaching the trace and the client's HAR when they provide it.

Vanessa
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T21:08:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: Urgent: intermittent 5xx + latency on streaming endpoint

Quick technical summary from my end after an hour of reproductions:

- Root cause: client-sdk-js dechunker retains a partial-header buffer across chunk reads. When the client sends multiple small chunks with interleaved CRLF sequences, our header parser sometimes misinterprets a CRLF inside a chunk as end-of-headers only after an extra read, causing a transient state where the runtime emits a parse error and tears down the stream.
- Trigger is more likely when Transfer-Encoding: chunked is combined with pseudo-headers and small (<=128B) chunks.
- Impact: one failing connection results in client retries that increase queue depth and P90 latency for other requests.

Proposed fix: add an atomic header-reassembly pass in the dechunker that waits for either "

" or a full header-length observation before invoking the parser. I have a hotfix branch (fix/dechunker-atomic-reassembly) ready with unit tests and a small integration test using MarketPlay's trace.

Plan:
- Hotfix build and staged rollout to Dedicated pool in ~3 hours (if Ops greenlights).
- Longer-term: rewrite dechunker state machine to be more resilient and add fuzzing for small-chunk scenarios.

I've attached the failing trace snippet and the PR link: https://redwood.internal/pull/5412

— Karthik
